candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care, printed p.20 > Assignment, Delegation and Supervision.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — assignment based on client needs and staff competency
candidate.educational_objective: Make nursing assignments based on client needs and verified staff competency, using appropriate supervision and resources rather than assuming licensure alone establishes specialty competence.

options.A: Assign the most unstable child because an unrestricted RN license establishes competence for every specialty assignment.
options.B: Give the nurse a full independent PICU assignment without first considering the nurse's competency for the assigned care.
options.C: Assign any available PICU workload and rely on the nurse to request help only after difficulty develops.
options.D: Match assigned care to client needs and the nurse's verified competency, with appropriate supervision and resources for the assigned tasks.

candidate.rationale: The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan places assignment, delegation, and supervision under Management of Care. It directs the nurse to identify assignments based on client needs, assign appropriate tasks to personnel with competency to perform them, supervise care provided by others, and evaluate staff ability based on allowable duties, competency, judgment, and decision-making. Therefore D is the safest approach. A incorrectly treats licensure as proof of specialty competence. B omits competency assessment before an independent high-acuity assignment. C delays use of supervision/resources until a problem has already developed.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Safe assignment requires matching client-care needs and tasks to personnel competency and using appropriate supervision; an RN license alone does not establish competency for every specialty task or assignment.
candidate.source_locator: Management of Care, printed p.20 > Assignment, Delegation and Supervision: identify tasks for assignment/delegation based on client needs; assign appropriate tasks based on client needs to personnel with competency to perform tasks; delegate and supervise care; evaluate staff ability to perform assigned tasks considering allowable duties, competency, judgment, and decision-making.
candidate.source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
candidate.stem: A medical-surgical RN is floated to a pediatric ICU where the nurse has not previously practiced. Which assignment approach is safest?
